name: Chinese · Phrases · Health and pharmacy
source: Phrases: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org) sentences written by native speakers, each linked in its src; lines marked generated were written for Lianki and checked for natural use

entries.back: What seems to be the problem?
entries.note: The doctor's opening question; also pharmacists. Answer with your symptoms.
Basic symptom line, to a doctor, pharmacist or family.
Explaining why you sound rough or are staying home.

entries.back: I've got a fever and I ache all over.
entries.note: Typical flu description to a doctor or boss.
Everyday word 嗓子 for throat; doctors write 喉咙.

entries.back: I've had a cough for days.
entries.note: Telling the doctor how long it's been; 好几天 = quite a few days.
To a friend or doctor; might mean you need to sit down.
The everyday, not crude, way to say it.
Nauseous; in other contexts 恶心 also means 'gross'.
Urgent warning; also said jokingly about something disgusting.

entries.term: 不好意思，我有点儿不舒服。
entries.back: Sorry, I'm not feeling very well.
entries.note: Excusing yourself from work, a meal or plans.
Concerned question to someone who looks off.

entries.reading: nǐ liǎnsè bù tài hǎo，méishì ba？
entries.back: You don't look so good. Are you OK?
entries.note: Friend's worried check-in; 病怏怏 = sickly and listless.

entries.back: You'd better go see a doctor.
entries.note: Friendly push to someone who keeps putting it off.

entries.back: I need to go to the hospital.
entries.note: In China people go to hospital outpatient clinics even for minor things.

entries.reading: nín hǎo，wǒ xiǎng guà gè hào
entries.back: Hi, I'd like to register to see a doctor.
entries.note: At the hospital registration desk; 挂号 is the first step of any visit.
Patient opening the consultation.
Doctor's question during a check-up.
Nurse or doctor; you'll be handed a thermometer.
Tell the doctor before any prescription.
Patient asking the doctor; IV drips (打点滴) are also common.

entries.back: Do you have anything for a fever?
entries.note: At the pharmacy counter.

entries.reading: zhè yào yī tiān chī jǐ cì？
entries.back: How many times a day do I take this?
entries.note: Asking the pharmacist or doctor about dosage.

entries.reading: fàn hòu chī，yī tiān sān cì
entries.back: Take it after meals, three times a day.
entries.note: Pharmacist's instructions; you'll hear this, not say it.

entries.back: This is for external use only.
entries.note: Pharmacist warning, also printed on labels.

entries.term: 我吃了药，一点用都没有。
entries.reading: wǒ chī le yào，yīdiǎn yòng dōu méiyǒu
entries.back: I took the medicine but it didn't help at all.
entries.note: Back at the doctor or complaining to family.
The classic Chinese advice for any illness; also a meme for lazy caring.
To someone who's sick or worn out.
Parents and grandparents say this constantly when it's cold.

entries.reading: tā bǎ gǎnmào chuán gěi wǒ le
entries.note: Blaming someone for passing on a bug.
Standard wish to someone sick, in person or in a message.
